ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In the circuit shown in the figure, what happens to the reading of ammeter \(A\) if the resistance \(R_1\) increases?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The upper and lower two wires in the figure form two common nodes; the left branch is an ideal current source labeled Ik; the middle branch is a variable resistor R1 directly connected between the upper and lower nodes; the right branch is an ammeter A in series with a fixed resistor R, also connected between the same pair of upper and lower nodes. Reasoning: The current source Ik provides a fixed total current, and this current divides between the R1 branch and the right-side R branch. If R1 increases, then the conductance of the R1 branch decreases, and the current through R1 decreases. Since the total current Ik is fixed, when less current flows through the middle branch, more current will flow through the right-side fixed resistor R branch. Therefore the reading of ammeter A increases.
